dialog.body: Zoning and Inspections, this is Anita. How can I help you?
Hi, yeah, um, I'm trying to figure out if I need a permit for a fence. Basically I've got a vegetable garden and the deer keep eating everything, so I want to put something up.
Okay, sure. Can I get your address first so I know where we're talking about?
Yeah, it's 188 Gibbs Avenue. Ocean Drive side.
Got it, 188 Gibbs. And what kind of fence are you thinking? Material, height, that kind of thing.

So, cedar. Basically about four and a half feet tall. Is that, like, under some limit where you don't need anything? I read something online but it was confusing, it seemed to say different things on different pages.

That's pretty common, the websites can be vague. In general a fence does need a permit in Newport, and height is one of the things we look at, along with where it sits on the lot. Is this around the garden only, or the whole yard?
Just the garden. It's in the back, like, a rectangle. Hang on one sec, [pause] buddy, check the couch cushions. Sorry, my kid lost a mitten and we're basically tearing the house apart.
Oh no, it's mitten season. Take your time. Is the garden near a property line, do you know?

Um, kind of? One side is maybe six feet from the neighbor's. So I'm not sure if that matters. Wait, so you're saying I do need a permit? Because I thought under like four feet was fine, and mine's four and a half, so that's over, right? Or is it the other way around?

I wouldn't hang it on a number like that. For a fence in the back of a residential lot, the safest answer is to plan on applying for a permit, and we'll confirm the details when you file. It's a short application and we'd want a simple sketch showing the fence and the property lines.
Okay. A sketch. Like, hand drawn is fine? Or does it need to be a survey thing?
Hand drawn with measurements is usually okay to start. If you have your plot plan from when you bought the house, that helps.

I might have that in a folder. [crosstalk] No, not that one, the other bin. Sorry. So, the contractor, I'm hiring somebody to build it. Does the contractor handle the permit, or is that me as the owner?

Either can do it. A lot of contractors pull the permit as part of the job, but you should ask them up front and get it in writing. If you're the homeowner, the permit is ultimately about your property, so you want to know it's been done.
Okay, so basically I ask them, do you pull the permit, yes or no. Got it. And if they say no then it's on me.
Right. Then you'd file it yourself, and you can do that here at the office.

Okay. And one more thing, there's the finished side thing. Like the good side of the fence. Does that have to face out, toward the neighbor, or can it face in toward my garden? I keep seeing people say different things.

That's a good question. Generally the finished side is expected to face outward, toward the neighbor or the street. But I'd confirm it on the application so you're not building it backwards. Do you know which side the contractor plans?
No, I haven't asked yet. I thought the posts and rails were supposed to be on the inside, no wait, is that the same thing? The finished side out means the flat boards show, right?
Yes, the smoother, flat face outward, and the posts and rails on your side. That's the usual way.
Okay, okay. I think I had it mixed up. So, permit, sketch, ask the contractor, finished side out. Is that everything?
That's the gist. Come by or call back once you have the sketch, and we can look it over. If you want, I can take your number in case someone needs to follow up.
Great, 401-555-0154. And it's Antonio?
Yeah, Antonio Amaral. A-M-A-R-A-L.
Perfect. Good luck with the mitten, and the deer.
Thanks. I'm still a little unsure about the height thing, but I'll bring the sketch in. Thanks a lot.
Anytime. Have a good afternoon.
